chapter: Chicago, Detroit and Seattle Harmony Kings
title: Hired by Eddie Niebaur's Seattle Harmony Kings
summary: Niebaur overhears them practising at Friars Inn and offers both trumpeters jobs starting after the band's notice period.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: No - the Seattle Harmony Kings - had checked in that "Friars Inn" the--- following the other band and he heard us practice in our room and he offered us a job---
Yeah - both of us, because he needed two. He needed two trumpets; his trumpet players---
Yeah - one trumpet player was named Handy and the other one---

Yeah --- and the other one was Earl -- got to be famous - he was from Philadelphia. But, anyway, those guys were leaving and they needed trumpet players. So, he said -- you know, you guys want the job, you got it. And, uh, you join us in a 30-day period or something at Castle Farm, Cincinnati. He said, you guys, you're all set to take the job. And, they were a Victor Recording artists and, so, the first--- well, of course, I haven't got there yet, but the first recording with those guys was "I'll Just Be Breezing With a Breeze" -- remember that song --"I'll be Breezing Along with a Breeze" -- you know. So, right after that, ---
Well, that was the time they hired you for a period in the future.
Yes, because those fellows gave their notice; they had about 30 days to go on the notice thing - you know---
